takeaways: A race condition appears when two or more processes access shared data without proper synchronization.
Peterson’s algorithm demonstrates that software alone can guarantee mutual exclusion for two processes.
Hardware atomic primitives such as test‑and‑set make lock implementation efficient on multiprocessors.
Mutexes and semaphores are the building blocks for synchronizing many threads in real applications.
Monitors provide a structured way to combine mutual exclusion with condition synchronization.
Deadlock occurs only when all four necessary conditions hold simultaneously.
Prevention, avoidance, detection and recovery form a hierarchy of strategies to keep systems deadlock‑free.
